analysis.title: Sticky inflation keeps the Fed on a hiking path
key_insights: US core CPI surprised to the upside for a third straight month. Services, rents and goods all rose more than expected. Core is 2.8% y/y, and the 3-month annualised rate is close to 4%, a trend pointing slightly up.
SEB's forecast is a Fed hike in December, reinforced by the CPI print, Waller's hawkish comment about a double hike and Friday's strong jobs report.
The US 2-year yield rose about 20bp. The market fully prices a 25bp December hike, with a 15% probability of a double hike.
US equities fell on the day: S&P 500 -0.4%, Nasdaq -0.7%, Nvidia -5.5%. European equities rose: Eurostoxx 50 +0.6%, OMXS30 +0.5%.
Brent trades around USD 92 per barrel. Hopes that the war with Iran is ending weigh on oil, while new attacks on ships keep part of the risk premium in place.

US, Ukraine and Russia held peace talks in Abu Dhabi, the first since February. The US called day one 'very productive', but the parties remain far apart on territory and security guarantees and expectations of a breakthrough are low.

Norwegian CPI-ATE fell to 2.7% in October, one tenth below SEB's forecast and in line with Norges Bank. Lower food and imported goods prices may reflect the stronger krone. Higher rents are an upside risk. SEB expects inflation to come in lower than Norges Bank projects.

Riksbank minutes were more hawkish than the press release and press conference. Jansson and Hjelm flagged upside inflation risks from energy and growth. Jansson and Seim left the door open to a December hike, and Governor Thedéen expects hikes in line with the September path over roughly six months.
SEB expects the Riksbank to hold in December and hike one last time in March, citing low October inflation, a stronger krona and lower energy prices.

Swedish private-sector output fell 0.5% in September after several months of gains. SEB expects 2026 GDP growth of 3.0%, with 2027 headwinds from costlier energy, higher mortgage rates and the end of support measures.

Swedish politics: Kristersson's exploratory mandate was extended to 17 November, and he needs a credible plan to bring the Centre Party on board. Without a new government, the caretaker government will present a neutral, pared-back budget.
The strong Democratic gains in the US midterms are pressuring Trump and the Republicans, as well as oil prices and AI investment.
